react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of eight differentially abundant metabolites reveals three convergent biological signals. The strongest consensus is selenium, which appears as a single-driver hit across three WikiPathways ORA results from RaMP-DB: rank 0 'Pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway' (WP:WP2848, FDR=0.00072), rank 1 'Ferroptosis' (WP:WP4313, FDR=0.00111), and rank 2 'Selenium micronutrient network' (WP:WP15, FDR=0.00205). Selenium atom (CHEBI:27568) is the sole intersecting metabolite across these three pathways, consistent with its essential role as a cofactor for selenocysteine-containing enzymes including glutathione peroxidases (GPX) and thioredoxin reductases (TXNRD) that regulate oxidative stress and ferroptosis. The second convergent signal is prostaglandin/thromboxane metabolism: mummichog's rank-0 hit is 'Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate' (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.0059) with three overlapping eicosanoids (thromboxane A2 as KEGG:C02198, plus prostaglandins H2/E2/D2/I2 at KEGG:C00427, C00584, C00696, C01312). Thromboxane A2 (C02198) is a direct arachidonic acid CYP/COX product that also appears in mummichog's rank-8 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' pathway. InChIKey reconciliation confirms that the input identifier RZWIIPASKMUIAC maps to the same first-block family as the mummichog thromboxane A2 entry, resolving a namespace artefact. The third signal is glucose-centered: mummichog consistently maps D-Glucose (C00221) to β-D-glucose within 'Glycolysis and Gluconeogenesis' (rank 2, p=0.0164) and related hexose-handling pathways, consistent with the glucose input. Together these results suggest that the treatment perturbs (1) selenium-dependent antioxidant defense and ferroptotic cell death, (2) eicosanoid-mediated inflammation/vasculature signaling, and (3) central carbohydrate metabolism.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of eight differentially abundant metabolites reveals three convergent biological signals. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-DB) identifies the Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15) at rank 2 (FDR=0.00205) driven by a single-input selenium hit; two additional selenium-related WikiPathways enrich in parallel — Pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway (WP:WP2848, rank 0, FDR=0.00072) and Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313, rank 1, FDR=0.00111). The mummichog m/z-direct method independently recovers the eicosanoid cluster as its top hit — Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.0041) — with thromboxane A2 (C02198) confirmed as a network-propagated hit in the prostaglandin H2 / thromboxane A2 branch of the arachidonic acid cascade. D-Glucose (C00221) appears as a rank-2 hit for Glycolysis and Gluconeogenesis (p=0.014) and rank-1 for N-Glycan biosynthesis, reflecting its central role in hexose metabolism. These three independent signals — selenium-dependent antioxidant biology, eicosanoid-mediated inflammation and vasculature signaling, and glucose-centred carbon metabolism — converge on treatment-perturbed redox-inflammatory and metabolic axes.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of eight differentially abundant metabolites identified three convergent biological signals. The mummichog m/z-direct method recovered prostaglandin formation from arachidonate as the top hit (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.00386), with thromboxane A2 (KEGG:C02198) confirmed as a network-propagated hit within this pathway cluster alongside prostaglandins H2, E2, D2 and I2. The RaMP-DB multi-database ORA independently identified the Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15) at rank 2 (FDR=0.00205), driven by the selenium atom (CHEBI:27568) as the sole input hit. Selenium also independently enriched in Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313, rank 1, FDR=0.00111) and the Pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway (WP:WP2848, rank 0, FDR=0.00072). D-Glucose (KEGG:C00221) emerged as a driver metabolite for the glucose metabolic cluster, appearing in N-Glycan biosynthesis (MUMM:n_glycan_biosynthesis, rank 1) and Glycolysis and Gluconeogenesis (MUMM:glycolysis_and_gluconeogenesis, rank 2) with matching mummichog p=0.02075. The convergent signal across prostaglandin-lipid signaling, selenium-dependent redox biology, and glucose metabolism suggests treatment-perturbed inflammation-vascular and metabolic axes.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of eight differentially abundant metabolites reveals three convergent biological signals. The strongest consensus is selenium, which appears as a single-driver hit across three WikiPathways ORA results from RaMP-DB: rank 0 'Pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway' (WP:WP2848, FDR=0.00072), rank 1 'Ferroptosis' (WP:WP4313, FDR=0.00111), and rank 2 'Selenium micronutrient network' (WP:WP15, FDR=0.00205). Selenium atom (CHEBI:27568) is the sole intersecting metabolite across these three pathways, consistent with its essential role as a cofactor for selenocysteine-containing enzymes including glutathione peroxidases (GPX) and thioredoxin reductases (TXNRD) that regulate oxidative stress and ferroptosis. The second convergent signal is prostaglandin/thromboxane metabolism: mummichog's rank-0 hit is 'Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate' (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.0059) with three overlapping eicosanoids (thromboxane A2 as KEGG:C02198, plus prostaglandins H2/E2/D2/I2 at KEGG:C00427, C00584, C00696, C01312). Thromboxane A2 (C02198) is a direct arachidonic acid CYP/COX product that also appears in mummichog's rank-8 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' pathway. InChIKey reconciliation confirms that the input identifier RZWIIPASKMUIAC maps to the same first-block family as the mummichog thromboxane A2 entry, resolving a namespace artefact. The third signal is glucose-centered: mummichog consistently maps D-Glucose (C00221) to β-D-glucose within 'Glycolysis and Gluconeogenesis' (rank 2, p=0.0164) and related hexose-handling pathways, consistent with the glucose input. Together these results suggest that the treatment perturbs (1) selenium-dependent antioxidant defense and ferroptotic cell death, (2) eicosanoid-mediated inflammation/vasculature signaling, and (3) central carbohydrate metabolism.
